note: Triennial rural district council election. Polling in Fermanagh took place on Wednesday 31 May 1933 and the results were declared on Thursday 1 June. Four divisions were contested; the remaining divisions were filled at the nominations. Filed on 1933-05-31, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Fermanagh that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1933-06-01 (verification 5 Nov 2026). The Impartial Reporter of 4 May 1933, p. 5, prints the nominations: five contests announced (Coolnamarrow, Castlebalfour, Lisnaskea, Belleisle, Mullynagowan) and twenty-six members returned unopposed, named by division (added 6 Nov 2026). Only four divisions went to a poll (Impartial Reporter, 8 June 1933, p. 7); Coolnamarrow, where two Nationalists (James Cassidy and James Moohan) were nominated, is held: no source read says which of them was returned. Kirkpatrick lost the seat by two votes though he had a majority of nine on paper. Majority 2. Nationalist gain.
